# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]
Fax: 859-425-3379

**From:** Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

---

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated August 4, 2026**
**Reference number:** POC-6E16FAD700-45453
**Member:** Quinn Jennings — **Member ID:** W670697505
**Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Aetna's denial of prior authorization for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), issued on August 4, 2026 under reference number POC-6E16FAD700-45453. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed, and the records in my file address the criteria in Aetna's own policy, CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy. Below, I set out each criterion in the plan's own words and point to where my records meet it.

## The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Conservative treatment and persistent symptoms**

The plan's policy states:

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

The policy then lists the treatments that trial is to include, among them:

> "Protective cushions/pads; Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded); Corticosteroid injections; Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions; Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs);"

My records establish the following:

- I have had **24 months of progressive foot pain that is not relieved by rest**.
- I took **NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief**.
- I received a **corticosteroid injection on March 25, 2026**, which gave only about **four weeks of partial relief**.
- I completed **activity modification, wide toe-box footwear and a custom orthotic from April 12, 2026 to June 21, 2026 — 18 visits**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- My records document that I **cannot tolerate closed shoes**.

**2. Footwear**

The plan's policy states:

> "Alternative or modified footwear that must include the following: Wearing well-fitting, low-heeled comfortable shoes made out of soft materials (e.g., canvas, cloth, soft leather) with wide toe box and padding; or"

and, in the alternative:

> "Lace-ups or a combination last (front of the shoe is wider than the back of the shoe) that conforms to the bunion and minimizes irritation; and"

My records document a trial of **wide toe-box footwear together with a custom orthotic**, supervised as part of my course of care. If Aetna needs a more specific description of the shoes I tried, my treating providers can supply it — that detail is [to be confirmed from the chart/treating provider].

**3. Radiographic confirmation**

The plan's policy states:

> "Radiographic confirmation Footnotes for Radiographic confirmation * of the most recent weight-bearing view X-ray demonstrating both of the following: An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) (formed by the long axis of the first and second metatarsals) of 12 degrees or greater; and"

My **weight-bearing foot radiographs taken June 29, 2026** show a **hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees** and an **intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees**. Both measurements exceed the thresholds the plan itself has published.

The policy also states:

> "Radiographic confirmation must include interpretation and report of weight bearing anterior/ posterior and lateral views of the affected foot."

My imaging was weight-bearing and was interpreted with the angle measurements reported above. If the radiology report as submitted did not include every view the policy calls for, I ask that Aetna tell me specifically which view or report element is missing so my provider can send it, rather than deny the request as incomplete.

**4. Skeletal maturity and additional findings**

The plan's policy states:

> "Documentation of skeletal maturity; and The member has one or more of the following:"

and among the findings that follow:

> "Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint; or"

> "Demonstration of osteoarthritis on X-ray, as evidenced by any of the following: Cysts in the metatarsal head; or Loss of the cartilage space between the bones; or Mild-to-moderate bony proliferative pathology; or"

My examination documents **positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain**. My records also note **ulceration risk over the prominence** and that I cannot tolerate closed shoes. On skeletal maturity, I am an adult and my date of birth is on file with Aetna; if a specific statement of skeletal maturity is required, that is [to be supplied by my treating provider on request].

## About the reason given for the denial

The denial notice does not identify which document, measurement or finding Aetna found missing. It states only that the submitted documentation was incomplete. The records summarized above were part of the prior authorization packet, and they address the duration of my symptoms, the conservative treatments I tried and their results, my weight-bearing X-ray angles, and my examination findings.

I also want to be straightforward with you about the limits of what I can quote. I have been able to quote only the portions of CPB 0629 available to me. Several of those passages end in a colon and introduce further lists of conditions that I have not been given, and the policy contains additional criteria I cannot reproduce here. I am therefore not in a position to state every threshold the plan applies. If Aetna relied on a criterion I have not addressed, I ask that the plan identify it by name so it can be answered directly.

I also note that my records do not describe a request for surgery on both feet at the same time, so the following provision does not appear to apply to my case:

> "Note: A bilateral bunionectomy done at the same time generally is not deemed medically necessary unless extenuating circumstances are present."

## What I am asking for

I respectfully ask Aetna to:

1. **Overturn the denial** of prior authorization for CPT 28296 and approve the procedure; or
2. If any item is still considered missing, **tell me in writing exactly which criterion in CPB 0629 was applied and which specific document, measurement or report is needed**, so my surgeon can provide it promptly; and
3. **Confirm receipt of this appeal in writing.**

I understand this appeal must be received by **January 31, 2027** (180 days from the date of the notice). I am submitting it using Aetna's Member Complaint and Appeal Form, available in my account at aetna.com under complaints, grievances and appeals, sent to the appeal address printed on my denial letter (fax 859-425-3379). If anything further is needed, I can be reached at [my phone number] or [my email address], and my surgeon's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone number].

Thank you for taking the time to review this again.

Sincerely,

 

_________________________
**Quinn Jennings**
Member ID: W670697505
Date of birth: [my date of birth]
Reference number: POC-6E16FAD700-45453
